source_excerpts.text:
## 1. The question created by the concept

Suppose an expensive stochastic computation has produced an actual value

\[
X\sim P.
\]

Other work may already depend on that particular realization. After a model change, we require an output

\[
Y\sim Q
\]

with exactly the new distribution, while disturbing \(X\) as little as possible.

If \(P\) and \(Q\) are fully known, ordinary coupling theory describes the best possible agreement. For a bit, the minimum disagreement is \(|p-q|\). But a coupling’s mathematical existence does not specify an operation available to someone who only has sampling access.

I therefore fixed the information contract:

1. The original, correctly distributed \(X\) is supplied.
2. Fresh independent draws from \(P\) and \(Q\) can be requested.
3. The procedure may adaptively choose which source to query and when to stop.
4. It receives no probabilities, densities, common random seed, or certificate that the two laws agree.
5. The same procedure must produce exactly \(Q\) for every pair of laws in the declared class.

The original sample is already paid for. All budgets below count **new source draws**.

This distinction matters for cached simulations and stochastic computation. Two output laws can be identical while the permitted interface supplies insufficient information to certify that copying an old realization is a valid universal operation. Conversely, a discrete outcome can sometimes be retained with a rigorously optimal sampling cost.

## 2. General theorem: exact reuse is limited to common atoms

Let the state space be standard Borel—for example, a finite set, the real line, or a Euclidean space. Require exactness for **all probability laws** on that space.

### Universal selection theorem

**Every universally exact procedure that terminates after finitely many queries almost surely must return a value that actually appeared among its target-source draws.**

This is a restriction derived from exactness; selection from the observed target samples is not assumed in advance.

The proof uses finite transcripts. Suppose a procedure sometimes stops and returns a value absent from its target-query list. Some finite query sequence has this property with positive probability. Fix a corresponding tuple of source values for which a positive-measure set of auxiliary random seeds produces that behaviour.

## 7. What survived comparison with existing descriptions

The strongest same-information comparator was empirical optimal transport. It survived: it is the optimal operation for fixed per-source budgets. The new work supplies the converse explaining why every universally exact method is constrained to its empirical marginals.

The contribution boundary is explicit:

| Existing work | What it already supplies | Result developed here |
|---|---|---|
| Astra N1415 | Actual recorded-bit excursion repair and exact repair on a supplied fixed binary computation graph | Sharp local resource laws and the general-state-space reuse boundary |
| Bernoulli factories, completeness and sequential information theory | Exact transformations of unknown probabilities, polynomial constraints and information inequalities | Matching bounds for disturbance of the distinguished old sample |
| Minibatch and expected-batch optimal transport | Empirical couplings, population marginal properties and transport calculations | Optimality over every universally exact procedure with the same fixed per-source information |
| Known-density maximal coupling | Exact maximal agreement with density access | An ideal benchmark whose stronger information is unavailable in the declared interface |
| Recent exact output-alignment work | Source sampling with a supplied target attribute law and sharp query-count results | Two unknown laws and the objective of retaining an actual old realization |

The minibatch antecedents include Fatras et al., Pooladian et al., and Boïté et al.; known-density maximal coupling is described by Jacob, O’Leary and Atchadé. The recent work of Jiang et al. is a particularly close access-model antecedent, although its target law and objective differ. :chatgpt-content-reference{index="4"}

The proofs were checked independently by collaborators. Computational verification used exact rational arithmetic for the finite absorbing chains, stopped path laws, callback traces and combinatorial identities. An independently formulated adaptive decision-tree linear programme matched the sharp hard-cap values for caps one through eight. The tolerance table’s integer thresholds were certified using directed numerical intervals.

These checks support the construction and calculations; the general claims rest on the proofs.

Finite precision changes literal equality. Quantized measurements have atoms; approximate displacement is a different objective.
The solved budget classes are precise. The binary hard-cap frontier is complete for every integer cap. Expected-budget sharpness is proved at odd budgets. General-space optimality is proved for fixed per-source budgets.

I regard this as a completed foundational result with provisional novelty. Its consequences for end-to-end scientific simulation or physical capability remain to be demonstrated; a civilisation-changing capability has not been established.

What has been established is that a stochastic model needs an additional description when reuse matters: the operations through which its law is accessible. That description determines whether a stored realization can be retained at all, and, for a bit, gives the exact attainable price of retaining it.
